fiction_notice: Original fiction. Not a real event, person, company or recording.

hooks.text: The camera has already recorded tonight.
hooks.note: Six words, a complete impossibility, zero setup. The strongest short hook in the batch.

hooks.text: At six in the evening, the camera already has tonight's footage.
hooks.note: Clearer, but the clause order buries the strange part until the end.

hooks.text: The camera records one hour of tomorrow. Every single day.
hooks.note: Good, but explains the rule before the viewer has felt the wrongness.

hook_rationale: Hook 1 lands the impossibility inside the first second and leaves a question the viewer cannot answer without the next line. The other two are more informative and less urgent, which is the wrong trade at second zero.
final_twist: The footage is not from the future. It is from an older camera sealed inside the wall that has been recording the new camera, and everything it sees, a day before anyone else does.
music_mood: Institutional quiet. A single fluorescent-pitched tone held throughout, bending very slowly downward. A second tone joins at 0:37 and the two beat against each other until the final cut.
sound_bed: Infrared filter clicks, chair scrapes, plaster breaking, and an electrical hum that only becomes audible once the cavity is open.
youtube_title: This Security Camera Records Tomorrow Night, One Hour At A Time
description: Original fiction - not a real event. A camera that holds tomorrow's footage, but only ever from two until three in the morning, and only from an angle it cannot reach. Part of an original digital-mystery series.
pinned_comment: Original fiction, written for this channel - no real building and no real footage. If the old camera is watching the new one, what has the new one been watching?
